newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Dole says Romania should persevere with NATO bid.
newsitem.headline: Dole says Romania should persevere with NATO bid.

text.p: Former U.S. Senator Bob Dole, Bill Clinton's Republican rival in last year's election, told Romania's new centrist leaders on Saturday to persevere with efforts to secure quick NATO membership for the Balkan country.

"It's fair to say that Romania has made remarkable progress since last November," he told reporters after meeting reformist President Emil Constantinescu, whose centrists ended the ex-communists' seven-year grip on power in last year's polls.
Dole was on a two-day stopover in Romania on the way to Bosnia, where he was sent on an official mission by Clinton.

The United States surprised its allies last week by saying that only three ex-communist states -- the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland -- should be invited to start membership talks at the alliance's July 8-9 summit in Madrid.

"The final decision has not been made, and that will be made in the next couple of weeks," Dole said. "My advice is just keep persevering," he told Constantinescu, who had led a high-profile campaign for his country's longshot admission bid.
France is among a number of European countries who want Romania and Slovenia to be included along with the three favourites.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi told Clinton at the Group of Seven summit in Denver on Saturday he had made a big mistake by excluding Romania and Slovenia from the first round.
Dole said there was consensus in both the Republican-diminated U.S. Congress and the Democratic Administration on strenghthening ties with Romania.
"Whatever the decision (at Madrid), we'll continue the strong relationship we have," he said.

Constantinescu, who hailed Dole as "an old friend of the Romanian people", will travel to Prague on Monday to address a North Atlantic Treaty Organisation security workshop, when he is expected to make a final appeal for admission but also lay the ground for a rapid second round of enlargement.
